Topics: cost per token, tokens/sec/$, caching savings, batching latency tradeoffs, dedicated pool sizing, VPC peering and egress constraints

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): alright thanks everyone for joining, we'll kick off — quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya (Odyssey): hi priya here, daniel here too — hi
[00:07] Daniel (Odyssey): yeah daniel, hey
[00:10] Luis (Redwood SE): luis as well, arman from solutions is here
[00:14] Arman (Redwood SE): hey all
[00:18] Maya: great, objective today is a focused econ pulse, specifically tokens per dollar and where caching and batching are giving you wins or pain points, and set concrete next steps. sound good?
[00:26] Priya: yes that's perfect — we've seen some good numbers but want to validate cost at scale, especially for morning spike where latency matters
[00:32] Tom (Odyssey): and also want to understand if dedicated makes sense vs hosted for our throughput patterns

[00:40] Luis: quick context — we ran three configs this week: hosted with default batching, hosted with prefix/KV caching enabled, and dedicated reserved pool with 4 gpus quantized int8. numbers are in the sheet i shared but i'll surface the highlights.
[00:55] [00:55] Luis: hosted default: about 12k tokens/hour per vcpu equivalent, cost ~ $0.15 per 1k tokens (note: transcription may show dollars differently), tokens/sec peaked ~ 20 tokens/sec average during tests
[01:10] Luis: with prefix caching on README-like prompts we saw effective token generation drop by 45% and effective tokens/sec per dollar improved by ~2.4x. caveat is for multi-turn where user-specific context isn't reusable caching less helpful
[01:25] Priya: that matches our internal probe — the knowledge base queries are very cache-friendly but chat flows are not
[01:30] Daniel: can you explain the 2.4x — is that because of fewer decoder steps or less model input?
[01:35] Luis: mostly fewer model input tokens — when the prefix is a large fixed doc we hit the KV cache and avoid re-encoding, so the per-request compute drops dramatically. also batching plays in because similar prefixes group better.
[01:48] Maya: to add, Redwood's automatic prefix caching will only cache identical prefix keys, so you get biggest wins if prompts are templated with variables separated out

[02:00] Sofia: technical Q — does caching stay in-memory on the cluster or is it persisted across nodes? we worry about warm-up after node restarts
[02:08] Arman: good question. cache is in-memory per serving node with optional shared redis-style layer for cross-node hits; if node restarts you see warm-up cost. for dedicated we can pin cache to fewer nodes to improve hit stability
[02:22] Sofia: okay that's helpful — we can plan for a sticky routing window during the morning spike to avoid warm-down

[02:30] Tom: when you say dedicated quantized int8 pool what latency tradeoff are we looking at? we need sub-300ms tail on single-turn FAQ answers
[02:38] Luis: in our tests quantized int8 reduced cost by ~38% vs fp16 and latency improved a bit on throughput but the tail p95 sometimes increased by ~30ms due to kernel selection variance; however for many prompt shapes p95 stayed <260ms.
[02:58] Daniel: so for sub-300ms P95 sounds feasible but depends on prompt length and batching. how does batching affect tail?
[03:05] Luis: batching increases throughput efficiency but will add latency to individual requests up to the batching window. we tune max_batch_latency to balance. in online mode we had max_batch_latency at 20ms which kept median low, but during spikes the batch sizes grew and p95 crept up.
[03:22] Priya: what's the tradeoff in tokens/sec/$ if we loosen max_batch_latency to 50ms? any rough numbers?
[03:27] Luis: loosening to 50ms increased tokens/sec/$ by ~15% in our sample, but p95 rose ~40ms. depends on your SLO — if 300ms p95 is acceptable you can capture the efficiency gains.

[03:40] Maya: another lever is adaptive batching + priority lanes — latency-sensitive requests can bypass large batches at a small cost, while background summarization can be batched heavily.
[03:50] Priya: Is that out-of-the-box or configuration work?
[03:53] Arman: config work — Redwood supports tagging routes and priority weights. we can demo config for you.

[04:00] Tom: on costs — can we get tokens/sec/$ normalized across the three test configs so we can present to execs?
[04:05] Luis: yes — short answer: hosted default baseline X, hosted+cache ~2.1X baseline, dedicated+quant ~2.6X baseline in our workload. sheet has absolute numbers, i'll paste a summary after the call.
[04:20] [04:20] Luis: note there's noise due to prompt distribution; when we ran the 'knowledge-base heavy' workload cache gains were ~3x but for 'chatty' flows it was only 1.1x.

[04:35] Priya: ok that's important — our traffic is 60/40 chat vs KB so we should weight numbers accordingly

[04:40] Daniel: also want to understand operational overhead of dedicated — e.g., autoscaling burst for unexpected traffic, and support windows for that tier
[04:47] Maya: dedicated supports autoscaling and burst capacity options; there is a committed base and you can enable burst which is billed differently. we'll include burst pricing scenarios in the updated pricing doc.

[04:58] Sofia: network egress — we need to keep internal traffic in VPC, how does peering affect egress charges?
[05:04] Arman: within same cloud region peering keeps traffic internal and reduces public egress. if you choose Redwood Private on VPC, data stays in customer's network and we don't route through public endpoints. we should map your infra and give exact estimates.

[05:20] Priya: any security/regulatory blockers for us? SOC2 was mentioned earlier, also audit logs for inference requests
[05:26] Maya: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and supports audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integration for key management. we'll attach the security pack to the email.

[05:40] Tom: circling back to caching — for multi-tenant scenarios will tenant keys leak or is the cache tenant-isolated?
[05:46] Arman: cache is tenant-scoped by default; we isolate by tenant and route requests accordingly. cross-tenant contamination isn't possible unless you opt into a shared cache pattern.

[05:58] [05:58] Luis: quick note on instrumentation — we measure tokens generated, tokens ingested, kv cache hits, p95 tail, and tokens/sec/$; we can push dashboard access to your team so you can slice by route.

[06:10] Priya: would love dashboard access — helps us validate and avoid back-and-forth on numbers

[06:20] Maya: we'll provision read-only viewing this week.

[06:25] Daniel: on the pricing doc — will you include committed discount tiers or just pay-as-you-go?
[06:30] Maya: we'll include both. sample: pay-as-you-go hosted baseline, dedicated commit tiers with stepping discounts, and burst pricing. We'll also show cost modeling examples for your 3 traffic patterns.

[06:44] Tom: one more on model variants — are there recommended quantization profiles for our LLM family? we test on a Llama-style open model
[06:51] Luis: for Llama-like models we recommend int8 quant with per-channel scales; for certain prompt shapes int4 can be efficient but requires validation because it can affect quality. we'll run paired evals on your prompt set.

[07:05] Priya: quality regressions are my main concern — can we gate cost saves behind an eval threshold? like max 1% delta on our BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics
[07:12] Arman: yes, Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring and can block automatic rollouts if metrics degrade beyond thresholds. we'll wire your evals into the pipeline.

[07:25] Maya: practical reconciliation — Luis, can you schedule the 24h run and include both hosted and dedicated arms so we get apples-to-apples? also include cache enabled/disabled for both.
[07:33] Luis: yes will schedule. need the prompt set from Priya to make it representative.

[07:40] Priya: i'll share top-3 prompt clusters and the traffic distribution by Thursday.

[07:46] Daniel: can we get a conservative monthly cost projection with 95th percentile peak? execs like conservative numbers.
[07:52] Maya: we'll provide conservative (95th), median, and optimistic scenarios.

[08:00] [08:00] Maya: quick live demo? or should we keep this as sync and follow up with the benchmark results and a config walkthrough next week?
[08:05] Priya: follow up next week works, demo later if needed

[08:10] Maya: ok, recap and next steps — list out action items.
